subject: Demo conclusions — prioritized model slate and qualification path
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@veloxhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Demo conclusions — prioritized model slate and qualification path

Alex — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap + our recommended next steps so the procurement and engineering teams have a clear runway.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary use case: multi-turn clinical triage assistant for patient intake (short structured prompts + long medical history context).
- Quality guardrail: >= 92% exact-medical-entity recognition on your sample set; hallucination risk must be low for medication advice.
- Latency target: p95 < 650ms for 512-token request; expected concurrency 12–15 req/s in peak.
- Data requirements: encrypted KV cache, SOC2 audit logs, and VPC/private deployment for PHI.

Our recommended prioritized model slate (shortlist):
1) LlamaX-13B-QLoRA (quantized) — "Favored". Best balance for your throughput needs: 13B with 4-bit quant produces acceptable latency at 512 tokens on our Dedicated profile, strong entity extraction with your prompt set after light instruction-tuning. Lower cost vs larger dense engines.
2) Aurora-7B-RT — "Latency-first". Smaller dense 7B engine optimized for real-time conversational throughput. Slightly lower factual recall on long histories but p95 latency consistently below 350ms. Good fallback for peak spikes or interactive clinician flows.
3) Titan-34B-OPT (fp16) — "Quality-first". Top quality on hallucination-sensitive prompts and long-context summaries, but highest cost and p95 latency ~900–1,100ms on typical Dedicated stacks. Recommend only for final post-processing (summaries/QA) or if quality trumps cost.

Why this slate? Shortlist gives you an operational path: Aurora for lowest latency, LlamaX as the cost/quality sweet spot for most production traffic, and Titan reserved for high-assurance completions. We recommend routing policies that prefer LlamaX by default, fall back to Aurora for sub-300ms SLOs, and route sensitive summary requests to Titan.

Attached: velox-prompt-pack-v1.zip (sample prompts + golden labels), benchmarks-velox-0305.pdf (mini-benchmark we ran against your sample set).

Next steps (proposal):
- We run a 2-week pilot on Dedicated (staging) with the three engines above; include 48-hour regression monitoring and 1 canonical prompt set from your team.
- Ops: Marissa to scope infra requirements and SOC2 cert mapping.
- Commercial: Ben to propose pilot pricing and reserved capacity options.

Can you confirm the pilot window (targeting week of Mar 20) and supply the two additional red-team prompts you mentioned? If that works we'll send a short MOU and schedule kickoff.

Thanks — Nikhil

--

1) On ">= 92% exact-medical-entity recognition" — that's our internal bar for triage routing. Does the 92% number apply to LlamaX out of the box or after the light instruction tuning you mentioned?
2) For the Titan summaries — do you expect we can do just-in-time routing (call Titan only on summary endpoints) without inflating the overall monthly spend significantly?

We can provide the two red-team prompts by EOD Friday. Week of Mar 20 works for a pilot kickoff for us — aim for Mar 21 start if possible.

Subject: Re: Demo conclusions — prioritized model slate and qualification path

Alex — short answers and operational detail so procurement/infra have concrete items.

1) 92% threshold: our mini-benchmark in the attached PDF reflects a two-step process. LlamaX-13B-QLoRA reached ~90% exact match out of the box on your sample set; after a light 2k-example instruction/label fine-tune (on your provided golden labels in velox-prompt-pack-v1.zip) we expect to reach the 92–95% range. We'll instrument the pilot to show delta.

2) Titan routing cost: yes — we recommend function-level routing. Only requests flagged for full-summary or compliance-checked responses route to Titan. Based on your estimated traffic profile (12–15 peak req/s), if 12% of requests are summaries you should see marginal cost increase of ~8–12% vs using LlamaX-only for everything. Ben's taking exact pricing below.

Operational checklist for pilot (what we'll deliver in the 2-week run):
- Dedicated pool provisioning (GPU SKU recommendations attached)
- Baseline regression harness with your prompt pack + 5 red-team prompts
- KV cache configuration and TTL suggestions for sensitive fields
- SOC2 evidence package mapping and initial compliance questionnaire answers
- Daily short-form test-run reports (latency p50/p95, token counts, cost estimate)

If Mar 21 looks good we'll send a one-page MOU and an infra reqs doc (AWS account/access, VPC peering steps).

--
Marissa Cole

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Demo conclusions — prioritized model slate and qualification path

Alex — cost/latency sketch for planning (estimates for pilot; final numbers in MOU). All numbers assume Dedicated capacity in us-west-2 and continuous 12 req/sec average with 15 req/sec peaks.

Estimated per-100k-request unit (512 tokens avg):
- Aurora-7B-RT: $1,200; p95 latency ~320–380ms
- LlamaX-13B-QLoRA (4-bit): $680; p95 latency ~520–680ms
- Titan-34B-OPT (fp16): $4,900; p95 latency ~920–1,100ms

Notes and guardrails:
- LlamaX is most cost-efficient for bulk inference; Aurora is a great latency burner for interactive flows; Titan should be used sparingly for quality-critical outputs.
- Autoscaling baseline: reserve 2x baseline throughput and 3x buffer for bursts for the pilot. We will publish token-level cost dashboards and route-level spend limits so you can cap Titan usage if needed.

Requested action items to proceed:
- Alex: send the two red-team prompts and confirm Mar 21 kickoff window.
- Velox procurement: quick review of the one-page MOU when it's available (I can pre-populate commercial terms).
- Marissa: I'll need the GPU SKU recs + estimated uptime SLA to lock pricing.

Happy to walk through these numbers in a 30m call if helpful.

--
